content_preview.title: What Four U.S. Coding-Model Releases Disclose: Licenses and Weight Access Differ, and Each Release's Benchmark Table Is the Vendor's Own
content_preview.summary: Beam and Ripple-65B list Apache 2.0, Muse Spark Open adds a $20 million Model-as-a-Service condition, and SWE-2 Flash keeps its weights private; each benchmark table is the vendor's own, run with differing setups.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

Four model releases aimed at coding and agent work were reported between October 5 and November 6, 2026, and each source places its model in a U.S. context. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/05/reflection-debuts-beam-a-open-weight-ai-model-to-rival-chinese-models-at-lower-compute-cost/) wrote on October 5 that Reflection AI, a Brooklyn-based startup, was unveiling Beam, a 501-billion-parameter model with 23 billion active parameters and a 1 million token context window, ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Analysis requirements met. Body 1854 words (script count; 1854 after stripping link URLs), inside the 800-2000 range. Nine sources, five outlets/evaluators independent of the four subjects. The piece examines two cross-cutting questions (what the weights permit; what the published benchmark numbers represent) rather than recapping one release. Structure separates facts (Background, Current situation) from the Herald's reading (Implications, explicitly labelled as the Herald's own reading, not forecasts or advice) and a closing list of what the sources do not establish. No Herald prediction or opinion found; the conditional 'would depend on a partner program whose eligibility The New Stack says is unclear' restates a reported unknown. Title is 136 characters, under the 150 limit. No Anthropic/Claude content remains: the Claude Haiku 5.5 clause from The New Stack is not reproduced, the competitor reference reads 'DeepSeek V4.1 Flash among them', which is accurate and not misleading. No relative dates: 'that month' is anchored to the October 5 TechCrunch article, 'the next few weeks' is a quoted attribution to the November 6 New Stack article.
editor_notes.source_verification: INDEPENDENT-SOURCE RECOUNT (strict): independent of the subjects = TechCrunch (Rebecca Bellan; own reporting: Axios corroboration, PitchBook funding, explicit statement that claims are unverified, Reflection did not respond; vendor figures relayed), SiliconANGLE (Duncan Riley; mostly relays Meta's launch table and licence summary, adds the Chinese-model comparison drawn from Meta's table; weakest on added reporting), VentureBeat (Carl Franzen; strongest: own checks of OpenRouter, Together and Fireworks pricing, card-versus-launch-graphic discrepancies, licence analysis, caveats on the lead), The New Stack (Amanda Caswell; relays Cognition's numbers but adds Apache 2.0 licence analysis, the ExploitBench caveat, outside commentary, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash outscoring Flash in Cognition's own table), Artificial Analysis (independent evaluator; the two pages count as ONE evaluator; it measures Beam and Muse Spark Open itself). That is 5 independent outlets/evaluators; counting only those that add their own reporting or measurement beyond relaying the vendor it is 4 (TechCrunch, VentureBeat, The New Stack, Artificial Analysis). Either way the Analysis minimum (4 sources, at least 2 independent) is met. The three Hugging Face model cards (Beam, Muse Spark Open, Ripple-65B Preview) are vendor documents and are correctly not counted as independent; SWE-2 Flash has no model card and its weights are private (The New Stack). Snapshots read from disk under sources/2026-11/what-four-us-coding-model-releases-disclose-licenses-and-weight-access-differ-and-each-releases-benchmark-table-is-the-vendors-own/: source-0 TechCrunch (confirmed: Oct 5 12:33 PM PDT; Brooklyn-based; 501B/23B active/1M context; weights 'this month'; claims not independently verified; Beam outscores Inkling on four coding tests where both report, Inkling multimodal and Beam text-only), source-1 SiliconANGLE (confirmed: Oct 15 update; editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Title and summary hold: 'Four U.S. Coding-Model Releases' (Beam: Brooklyn-based Reflection per TechCrunch; Muse Spark Open: 'U.S. lab' per SiliconANGLE; Ripple: 'American victory' and 'U.S.' per VentureBeat; SWE-2 Flash: 'fully American' per Cognition via The New Stack); 'Licenses and Weight Access Differ' (Beam and Ripple Apache 2.0 per card and LICENSE text; Muse Model License with label and Model-as-a-Service clauses; SWE-2 Flash private weights, base Apache 2.0, 'sits well within the company's rights' is The New Stack's statement, not Cognition's); 'Each Release's Benchmark Table Is the Vendor's Own' holds for all four (Reflection, Meta and Ricursive cards; Cognition's 'own benchmark table' per The New Stack, whose table the Herald did not see directly and does not claim to). The Ripple two-row Terminal-Bench 2.1 table, the rank swap, the Beam numerics columns, the Artificial Analysis scores (25 versus 18, v5.0.1), the 276B/12B Inkling-Small figures and the calendar inference for SWE-2 Flash's release are all verified. The 'Herald's own' labels on the licence grouping and the table ranking are present. Lists are marked 'among' or 'such as' where incomplete; 'Among the sources cited here, none reports an independent run of Ripple-65B Preview or SWE-2 Flash' is correctly scoped and confirmed against all nine sources plus the live Artificial Analysis model list. Two points fall short of complete and are recorded as clarifications in the corrections file: (1) the Muse Spark Open card links 'our report' to Meta's 'Muse Spark Open Evaluation Methodology' (PDF, October 2026), which the article neither cites nor reads. It states that Meta took every Terminal-Bench 2.1 result except Beam's from Artificial Analysis (Terminus 2 harness, E2B sandbox) and used Beam's self-reported figure with the harness unspecified, so Meta's 76.4 is an Artificial Analysis-sourced figure compiled in Meta's table rather than a Meta-run score, and the article's contrast of 'Meta's card' with 'independent' measurement and its statement that the sources do not explain the 76.4 versus 78.7 gap are incomplete. (2) The same document names the Intelligence Index behind the 39 as v4.3 (ten evaluations), sourced from Artificial Analysis on October 7, 2026, so the article's 'without naming an index version' is true of the card page but not of its linked report; and the SiliconANGLE-attributed 'full evaluation report still to come' (October 15) may be superseded by that document, which the article does not establish either way. Minor wording, not corrected: 'the fine-tune built on it' for SWE-2 Flash, where The New Stack describes a mid-training stage plus reinforcement learning on Inkling-Small.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Vendor claims are attributed ('claims', 'reports', 'states'), reported caveats are carried through, and the Implications section keeps to what the cited texts say. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Cross-release comparison of licences, weight access and benchmark provenance; no overlap with existing coverage. Related Herald pieces (Ripple-65B Preview News article, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Mistral Large 4) cover single releases or one licence clause; this article adds the Muse Spark Open licence text, the SWE-2 Flash private-weights question and the Ripple card's dual Terminal-Bench rows. The Herald's Nov 7 Inkling 2 Small piece covers a different model.
concerns: Two clarifications (not factual reversals) arising from Meta's evaluation-methodology document linked from the Muse Spark Open card but not cited: provenance of the 76.4 Terminal-Bench 2.1 figure (Artificial Analysis-sourced, Terminus 2, E2B) and the Index version behind Meta's 39 (v4.3, sourced October 7); filed in the corrections record.
The New Stack snapshot failed (HTTP 403); verification rests on a live text-reader rendering plus the Herald's own quote check; the page is not archived in the provenance snapshot.
'fine-tune' as a descriptor of SWE-2 Flash is the Herald's wording; The New Stack says 'built on' with mid-training and reinforcement learning. Minor, not corrected.
recommendations: Writers comparing vendor benchmark tables should follow the 'our report' or methodology link on a model card to see which numbers were run by the vendor, taken from a third-party leaderboard, or copied from another vendor's launch post.
Archive The New Stack pages through a fallback when the fetcher is blocked.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A careful, well-sourced Analysis that meets the length, source-count and independence requirements and whose headline claims all verify against raw source text; two clarifications about the provenance of Meta's Terminal-Bench figure and Index version are filed in a corrections record. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid licence and benchmark-provenance comparison for developers choosing open-weight coding models, not an industry-changing story
